---
name: menu-loader
description: Guide for creating and editing .menu.yaml files that define dynamic VS Code menus. Covers the YAML schema, action types (command, shell, snippet, url, chat, clipboard), when-clauses, menu location IDs, and developer tools for command discovery and validation. Use when the user wants to add, edit, or debug custom menus defined in YAML. Also use when asked about menu organization, command discoverability, or the vscode-native menu templates.
---

The **menu-loader** extension scans `.menu.yaml` files from `~/.vscode/menus/` (global) and `.vscode/menus/` (per-workspace) and builds live VS Code menus at runtime. Read the companion reference files before writing YAML:

- **[YAML-FORMAT.md](.github/skills/menu-loader/YAML-FORMAT.md)** — complete schema, every field, every action type
- **[SAMPLES.md](.github/skills/menu-loader/SAMPLES.md)** — annotated examples covering all patterns

---

## Existing Menu Templates

The workspace has a set of curated menus for VS Code's built-in commands in **`.vscode/menus/vscode-native/`**. Use these as **reference templates** when creating new menus:

| File | Target | Demonstrates |
|---|---|---|
| `typescript.menu.yaml` | MenubarMainMenu (conditional) | Language menu with imports, navigate, refactor, format, server, AI sections |
| `javascript.menu.yaml` | MenubarMainMenu (conditional) | Same structure as TypeScript, slightly different commands |
| `html-css.menu.yaml` | MenubarMainMenu (conditional) | Multi-language when-clause, Emmet integration |
| `json.menu.yaml` | MenubarMainMenu (conditional) | Small language menu with validate, format, convert |
| `markdown.menu.yaml` | MenubarMainMenu (conditional) | Snippets for formatting, preview commands |
| `yaml.menu.yaml` | MenubarMainMenu (conditional) | Format, fold, convert, AI sections |
| `notebook.menu.yaml` | MenubarMainMenu (conditional) | Cell operations, execution, output management |
| `git.menu.yaml` | MenubarMainMenu (always) | Cross-cutting tool menu (stage, branch, remote, stash) |
| `edit-enhancements.menu.yaml` | MenubarEditMenu | Injecting into built-in Edit menu |
| `go-enhancements.menu.yaml` | MenubarGoMenu | Injecting testing + tasks into Go menu |
| `view-enhancements.menu.yaml` | MenubarViewMenu | Injecting folding + display into View menu |
| `help-enhancements.menu.yaml` | MenubarHelpMenu | Injecting Developer submenu into Help menu |

The plan and conventions are documented in **`.vscode/menus/vscode-native/README.md`**.

## How Copilot Gets Live Data

The developer tools write their output to **`.vscode/menus/.cache/`** as markdown files on disk. This means YOU (Copilot) can read them directly using your file tools.

### Cache files

| File | Contents | Generated by |
|---|---|---|
| `.vscode/menus/.cache/commands.md` | All registered command IDs grouped by extension | `menuLoader.listCommands` |
| `.vscode/menus/.cache/menu-ids.md` | All known menu location IDs with descriptions | `menuLoader.listMenuIds` |
| `.vscode/menus/.cache/menu-tree.md` | Tree visualization of loaded `.menu.yaml` files | `menuLoader.showMenuTree` |
| `.vscode/menus/.cache/validation.md` | Validation report for all `.menu.yaml` files | `menuLoader.validateMenus` |
| `.vscode/menus/.cache/duplicates.md` | Duplicate command detection across all menu sources | `menuLoader.checkDuplicates` |

### Bootstrap workflow

If the user asks you to help write or edit a `.menu.yaml` and the cache files don't exist yet, tell the user:

> **Run "Menu Loader: Generate Cache for Copilot" from the Command Palette** (command: `menuLoader.dumpAll`). This generates all cache files at once. Then ask me again.

If the cache files already exist, **read them** to discover command IDs and menu locations before writing YAML. The files are at `.vscode/menus/.cache/commands.md` and `.vscode/menus/.cache/menu-ids.md`.

### After editing YAML

Tell the user to run **"Menu Loader: Validate Menu Files"** (`menuLoader.validateMenus`) again, then read `.vscode/menus/.cache/validation.md` to check for issues. Or the user can run **"Menu Loader: Generate Cache for Copilot"** (`menuLoader.dumpAll`) to refresh all files.

## Writing the YAML File

Create a `.menu.yaml` file in `.vscode/menus/` (project-local) or `~/.vscode/menus/` (global). See [YAML-FORMAT.md](.github/skills/menu-loader/YAML-FORMAT.md) for the full schema. Minimal example:

```yaml
name: my-menu
menu: MenubarMainMenu
title: My Menu

items:
  - group: 1_main
    items:
      - title: Do Something
        command: myExtension.doSomething
```

`order` is **optional on leaf items** — when omitted, items are ordered by their position in the YAML file (1-based). You only need explicit `order` when interleaving with built-in menu items.

### Relative positioning

Use the `position` field to place a menu relative to an existing item without knowing its exact group/order:

```yaml
# Place this entire dropdown right after the Selection menu
name: typescript
menu: MenubarMainMenu
title: TypeScript
position: "$Selection"

# Place a node after a specific built-in command
- position: "$#editor.action.clipboardPasteAction"
  title: Paste Special
  items:
    - title: Paste As…
      command: editor.action.pasteAs
```

| Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `$Title` | Place **after** the item titled "Title" |
| `^Title` | Place **before** the item titled "Title" |
| `$#commandId` | Place after the item with that command ID |
| `^#commandId` | Place before the item with that command ID |

## Developer Tool Commands Reference

| Command | ID | Purpose | Cache file |
|---|---|---|---|
| **List All Commands** | `menuLoader.listCommands` | All registered command IDs grouped by extension | `commands.md` |
| **Show Menu Tree** | `menuLoader.showMenuTree` | Tree visualization of loaded menus | `menu-tree.md` |
| **Validate Menu Files** | `menuLoader.validateMenus` | Validation report for all YAML files | `validation.md` |
| **List Menu Location IDs** | `menuLoader.listMenuIds` | All known menu IDs with descriptions | `menu-ids.md` |
| **Generate Cache for Copilot** | `menuLoader.dumpAll` | Runs all five above, writes all cache files | all of the above |
| **Check for Duplicates** | `menuLoader.checkDuplicates` | Detect commands duplicated across extensions and YAML menus | `duplicates.md` |
| **Reload Menus** | `menuLoader.reload` | Force re-scan and rebuild menus from YAML | (none) |
| **Open Menus Folder** | `menuLoader.openMenusFolder` | Reveal the menus directory in the Explorer | (none) |
| **Create Menu with Copilot** | `menuLoader.createMenu` | Open Copilot Chat with a menu-builder prompt | (none) |

All tools write output to `.vscode/menus/.cache/` AND open the file for the user to view.

The menu-loader tools are also available from the menu bar: **View → Menu Layout** submenu.

## Key Design Patterns

### When-clauses
Every level of the tree (`MenuDefinitionYaml`, groups, items) supports a `when` field. The runtime evaluates these against the current editor context.

#### Choosing the right condition

**Prefer `editorLangId`** when a language ID exists for the file type. It is the most reliable condition for menu-bar menus and is independent of file extension:
```yaml
when: "editorLangId == yaml"       # ✅ Best — covers .yaml, .yml, and untitled YAML files
```

**Use `resourceExtname`** for finer-grained triggering when you need to distinguish between files that share the same language ID, or when no language ID exists:
```yaml
when: "resourceExtname == .yaml"   # Triggers only for .yaml, not .yml
when: "resourceExtname == .menu.yaml"  # Only for menu definition files
```

**Use `resourceFilename`** for exact filename matches:
```yaml
when: "resourceFilename == Dockerfile"  # Only Dockerfiles (no extension)
when: "resourceFilename == package.json"  # Only package.json files
```

**Combine conditions** for maximum precision:
```yaml
when: "editorLangId == yaml && resourceExtname == .yml"  # YAML language, .yml extension only
```

#### Common patterns

| Pattern | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `editorLangId == markdown` | Active editor is Markdown |
| `resourceExtname == .ts` | Active file has `.ts` extension |
| `hasExtension(publisher.name)` | A specific extension is installed |
| `workspaceContains(**/*.py)` | Workspace has Python files |
| `isWindows` / `isMac` / `isLinux` | Platform check |
| `editorHasSelection` | Text is selected in editor |
| `configValue(editor.wordWrap) == on` | A setting has a specific value |

Combine with `&&`, `||`, `!`: `editorLangId == markdown && hasExtension(yzhang.markdown-all-in-one)`

### Six action types (mutually exclusive per leaf item)

| Field | Runs | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `command` | A VS Code command | `command: editor.action.formatDocument` |
| `shell` | A terminal command | `shell: "npm run build"` |
| `snippet` | Inserts a snippet | `snippet: "**${TM_SELECTED_TEXT}**"` |
| `url` | Opens a browser URL | `url: "https://example.com"` |
| `chat` | Opens Copilot Chat | `chat: "Explain this code"` |
| `clipboard` | Copies text to clipboard | `clipboard: "${file}"` |

### Variable expansion
Action values support `${variable}` placeholders resolved at execution time:
`${workspaceFolder}`, `${workspaceFolderBasename}`, `${file}`, `${fileBasename}`, `${fileDirname}`, `${fileExtname}`, `${selectedText}`, `${lineNumber}`, `${clipboard}`, `${env:NAME}`

### Menu locations (most common)
- `MenubarMainMenu` — create a **new** top-level dropdown
- `MenubarFileMenu`, `MenubarEditMenu`, etc. — inject into an **existing** menu
- `EditorContext` — editor right-click menu
- `ExplorerContext` — file explorer right-click
- `window/toolbar` — toolbar strip (proposed API)

Read `.vscode/menus/.cache/menu-ids.md` for the full list with descriptions.

### Tree structure
```
MenuDefinitionYaml          ← top-level: name, menu, title, when, items
  └── items[]               ← array of MenuNodeYaml
        ├── group node      ← has group + items[], creates separator section (depth 0) or submenu (depth > 0)
        ├── submenu node    ← has title + items[], no action
        └── leaf node       ← has title + exactly one action field
```

### Standard group template for language menus
Each language menu should follow this consistent group order:

```yaml
items:
  # 1_imports    — Organize imports, add missing imports
  # 2_navigate   — Go-to, symbols, references, call hierarchy
  # 3_refactor   — Rename, extract, code actions, quick fix
  # 4_format     — Format, comments, indentation
  # 5_project    — Project config, server, language version
  # 9_ai         — Chat/AI-assisted actions (when Copilot installed)
```

Groups may be omitted if empty for that language. Use `when: "hasExtension(GitHub.copilot-chat)"` on the `9_ai` group.

---

## Common Mistakes

1. **Wrong menu ID** — Use `MenubarMainMenu` (not `MainMenu`, not `menubar`). Check `.vscode/menus/.cache/menu-ids.md`.
2. **Multiple actions on one item** — Each leaf must have exactly ONE of: `command`, `shell`, `snippet`, `url`, `chat`, `clipboard`.
3. **Missing `name` or `menu`** — Both are required at the top level. `name` is the internal identifier; `menu` is where it appears.
4. **Command not showing up** — The extension owning the command may not have activated. Use `when: "hasExtension(publisher.name)"` to guard conditional items.
5. **Forgetting `title` on leaf items** — Without `title`, the raw command ID is used as the label.
6. **YAML indentation** — Use consistent 2-space indentation. Items must be nested under their parent's `items:` key.
7. **Duplicating text-toolkit items** — The `text-toolkit` extension already builds 10 submenus under Edit → group `9_text` (Convert Case, Line Operations, Sort, EOL Conversion, Blank Operations, Copy Filename, Line Filtering, Sequence & Numbering, Join/Split, Alignment). Do not add these to your Edit menu YAML.
8. **Duplicating built-in menu items** — Commands already in the stock VS Code pulldown menus (File, Edit, Selection, View, Go, Run, Terminal, Help) should not be re-added unless there's a language-specific context that improves discoverability (e.g. "Format Document" in a TypeScript menu is fine).

---

## Menu-Worthiness Criteria

Not every command belongs in a menu. A command is menu-worthy when **all** of these apply:

1. **User-facing** — it does something a person would deliberately invoke (not internal plumbing like `editor.cancelOperation`)
2. **Not already prominent** — it isn't already a primary keyboard shortcut every user knows (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+Z), unless grouping related items makes it strange to omit
3. **Not already in a pulldown menu** — if the command already appears in a VS Code built-in menu or text-toolkit's Edit submenus, don't re-add it unless language-specific context adds discoverability
4. **Discoverable value** — putting it in a menu helps people *find* it. Niche commands nobody looks for don't deserve menu space
5. **Contextually relevant** — it makes sense where the menu appears (language-specific commands only for that language)

---

## Menu Design Workflow

Follow this process every time a user asks for a new menu. Don't skip steps.

### Step 1 — Clarify the request
Before touching any files, make sure you understand:
- What file type / language / context is this menu for?
- Should it appear in the menu bar, right-click context, editor title bar, etc.?
- Is there an existing menu that partially covers this (Git, Markdown, …)?
- Are there specific extensions the user has installed that should be leveraged?

### Step 2 — Generate the command cache
Run `menuLoader.dumpAll` (or tell the user to run it if not available yet). This writes:
- `.vscode/menus/.cache/commands.md` — every registered command
- `.vscode/menus/.cache/menu-tree.md` — all currently loaded menus
- `.vscode/menus/.cache/menu-ids.md` — all valid `menu:` targets
- `.vscode/menus/.cache/validation.md` — current validation state

### Step 3 — Filter commands by topic
The commands list is large (3000+). Use `grep_search` with keyword patterns to extract relevant commands before reading everything:
```
grep: yaml|json|schema|lint|format   ← example for a YAML menu
grep: typescript\.|javascript\.       ← example for TS/JS extension commands
grep: editor\.action\.(rename|organizeImports|refactor)  ← editor actions
grep: emmet\.                         ← Emmet commands
grep: notebook\.(cell|execute|clear)  ← notebook commands
grep: ^\\| \`git\\.                   ← Git extension commands (in table format)
```
Read the full extension sections for any installed extensions that are directly relevant.

**Tip:** The commands.md file has two formats — extension commands are in markdown tables (`| command | title |`) and core commands are bullet lists (`- command.id`). Adjust your grep patterns accordingly.

### Step 4 — Categorise candidates (show this to the user before writing YAML)
Produce four labelled lists:

| Category | Criteria |
|---|---|
| ✅ **Include** | Directly relevant, adds clear value, not already in a stock VS Code menu |
| ❓ **Uncertain** | Useful but debatable — might duplicate a built-in, or only relevant to some users |
| ↔ **Related but exclude** | Tangentially related; belongs to a different menu or already well-covered elsewhere |
| 💡 **Non-command suggestions** | Snippets, `chat:` prompts, `url:` links, `shell:` scripts — things with no command ID |

### Step 5 — Check for duplication with built-in menus
Read `.vscode/menus/.cache/duplicates.md` (generated by `menuLoader.checkDuplicates` or `menuLoader.dumpAll`). This report shows:
- Commands from your YAML that also appear in extension menu contributions
- Whether their when-clauses are **mutually exclusive** (\u2705 OK) or **overlapping** (\u26A0 may duplicate)

If the duplicates report is not yet generated, tell the user to run **"Menu Loader: Generate Cache for Copilot"** (`menuLoader.dumpAll`).

**Rules for handling duplicates:**
- \u2705 **Mutually exclusive** when-clauses → safe to keep both (they won't appear simultaneously)
- \u26A0 **Overlapping** → remove the YAML entry unless there's a specific context-relevant reason to keep it
- **Generic text operations** (sort lines, join lines, case transforms) almost never belong in a language-specific menu — they're already in Edit/Selection menus
- Commands already in stock VS Code menus are OK to include if they're the "most common action" for that file type (e.g. Format Document in a language-specific menu)

> ⚠️ **TODO (menu-loader):** A future `menuLoader.diffWithBuiltins` tool should automate step 5 by comparing candidate commands against the built-in menu registrations.

### Step 6 — Present the plan and get feedback
Show the user the four categorised lists and your `menu:` / `when:` choices. **Do not write the YAML file yet.** Wait for the user to confirm, adjust or reject items.

### Step 7 — Write the YAML and show the tree
After approval:
1. Write (or update) the `.menu.yaml` file.
2. Run `menuLoader.dumpAll` to refresh all cache files.
3. Read `.vscode/menus/.cache/menu-tree.md` and paste the relevant tree block into the chat as a preview.
4. Read `.vscode/menus/.cache/validation.md` — fix any ⚠ errors (ℹ info notices for uninstalled extensions are expected and acceptable).

### Step 8 — when-clause tips
- For **menu-bar** menus prefer `editorLangId == yaml` over `resourceExtname == .yaml` — the language-id key works reliably in the menu bar and covers all file extensions mapped to that language.
- Use `resourceExtname` when you need **finer-grained** control (e.g. `.yaml` vs `.yml`, or `.menu.yaml` specifically).
- Use `resourceFilename` for **exact filename** matches (e.g. `Dockerfile`, `package.json`).
- For **context menus** (right-click) `resourceExtname` and `explorerResourceIsFolder` work well.
- Guard optional-extension items with `hasExtension(publisher.extensionId)` so they silently hide when the extension is absent.
